_sky: Day / night light: [minute of the day, colour], linear in between, multiplied over the outdoor picture (then times the weather tint). 7:00..16:00 is plain daylight; dusk runs warm (17:30) through mauve (18:30) to the night blue by 20:30, and dawn back from 4:30 to 7:00. The night blue is dark but keeps the farmer, the paths and the houses readable. It was 404c8e (luminance 0.31) until the real lamps ("lamps" below) came; 46529a (0.33) is a touch lighter, as the warm light near the houses now carries more of the night picture.
_sun: The sun of the 3D view outdoors (Game.sun_light). keys: [minute of the day, elevation (degrees above the ground), yaw (the light's rotation, degrees: -40 shines from the left of the screen, 0 from the front left (lower left), -90 from the back left (upper left)), colour, energy], linear in between. It rises low and orange from the lower left at 5:30, climbs golden through the morning, stands high and plain (the measured colour of SnowLayer.SUN_SHARE) at midday, and sinks golden to the back left, so the morning's long shadows fall up the screen to the right and the evening's down it to the right. After sunset (shadows already gone under the dusk tint) it eases back to `plain` by 20:30 and leaves it again from 4:00 to sunrise, so the night looks as it did before. plain: [elevation, yaw, colour, energy], the fixed sun of the night, the rooms and the mine (Main3D SUN_COLOR / SUN_ENERGY). The energy stays at plain's so the ground keeps its measured brightness; a clouded sky (weather_fx.json sun 0) keeps the plain colour.
_windows: Lit windows of the farmhouse and the village houses (3D view, drawn over the night tint). They glow with the dark: none while 1 - luminance of the light is under dark_from, full from dark_full. They are lit only in the hours listed ([from, to) minutes): from the afternoon to half past midnight and again at dawn. pane = how strongly the paper pane is lit, halo = the soft glow round it, halo_size = its width in window widths.
_pools: Warm light on the ground at night (3D view), as bright as the windows glow (windows above, the same dusk / dawn rise and lit hours). window: a pool in front of every lit window and shoji door, against its wall, `wide` window widths across (at least min_wide cells), reaching 2 * out cells from the wall; strength is how much warm light its middle gets (a door, bigger, up to 1.5 times it). color: the pools' light, a deeper orange than the panes so the lit ground reads warm over the night blue. lamp: the stone lanterns, a pool `radius` cells round the foot, a glow round the fire box (glow = its strength, glow_size = its width in cells). The pools' edges fall off in dithered steps, like the mine lantern's.
_wall_wash: pools.wall: warm light on the pale walls round every lit window and shoji door (3D view), added over the night tint like the pools, on the same schedule. Why: the tint multiplies the picture after the lights, so nothing drawn under it can be brighter than the tint itself (46529a at night); white plaster already sits near that cap under the night sun, so the real lamps ("lamps") can barely lift it, while dark wood takes them well. The wash is a soft disc on the window's wall plane, `reach` cells round the window's middle (from the ground to `up` over the window), its edge in dithered steps; a door's (bigger) up to 1.5 times as strong, like the pools. It lands only on pale pixels: as much as the picture's blue over the tint's blue (about the surface's brightness before the tint) lies between pale_from and pale_full, so the plaster and the paper take it and the dark boards, posts, eaves, roof and the ground under it (lit by the real lamps and the pools) do not. Figures in front are drawn back from the copy as for the glows. finishes: the village walls that are not plaster get their own wash (NightLights.finish_wash), as their red already sits at the tint's cap and the real lamps cannot lift it: `earth` the timber look's earthen plaster (a soft warm glow), `board` the yakisugi look's charred boards (a faint warm-grey sheen, so they stay dark wood, not orange). The same disc round the window, cut geometrically to the material (clear of the posts, the rails and the beam, within the wall's ends) and kept by the shader to the warm pixels: the copy's red over the tint's red above both its green and blue by warm_from .. warm_full (earth and wood; not the blue roof tiles, the grass or the sky), and not pale (the plaster has its own). lamp: a stone lantern standing in front of a house wall (one with lit windows; NightLights.lamp_walls / lamp_wash) washes it too, the same kind of disc centred on the point of the wall square to its fire box, `reach` cells round it (smaller than a window's), the strength and colour of that wall's material (plaster, earth, board) times `share`, fading linearly to nothing `out` cells from the wall; cut to the wall's ends, the finish's bands and posts, and round the panes; a building between the fire box and the wall drops it. Why weaker: a lantern's fire box is a small light, a window a whole lit room.
_festival_pools: pools.festival: the ground round a festival's lights (FestivalProps.glows) while it is on, as strong as its lights stand out (FestivalGlow.darkness), in both views. A standing lantern, the drum stage and the bonfire light a round pool `radius` times the glow's size; a string lantern hangs high, so its pool is `line` times as strong; a stall's lantern lights the ground in front of its counter instead: as wide as the stall plus 0.4, from the stall's middle `stall_front` cells forward, reaching `stall_reach` either way.
_sprite_shadows: How the figures (farmer, villagers, animals) and the field's objects get shadows in the 3D view (SpriteShadow). mode: "real" = a shadow-only caster quad wearing the sprite's picture, turned square to the sun, so the sun's shadow map throws the real silhouette (long in the morning and evening, short at noon, falling like the buildings' shadows), plus a faint contact blob; "blob" = the old flat dark oval only, at full strength always (the way back: set it and nothing else changes; `-- --sprite-shadows=blob` does it for one run). Why real: a billboard casts a thin wrong sliver of its own, but this quad stays steady under any lens; and the blob's direction never agreed with the buildings'. Where there is no sun (rain, night, rooms, the mine) the blob stays whole as the figure's shadow. blob_in_sun: the share of the blob left while the sun's shadows are at full strength (SpriteShadow.blob_share); blob_width: the blob's width as a share of the sprite's opaque width (read from its texture, so any sprite size fits); blob_depth: its depth as a share of its width; blob_min: its smallest width in cells.
_lamps: Real warm lights in the 3D view (NightLamps: OmniLight3D, no shadows) at the lit windows and shoji doors, the stone lanterns and the festival lights, so the lit meshes near them (walls, eaves, posts, trees, the stalls' counters) take warm light. The ground, the water and the grass are left out (their light is the drawn pools). At most `max` lights, the ones nearest the middle of the view, the farthest fading out before it is dropped (`fade` cells), so none pops. Brightness: `window` / `lamp` times Game.window_light, `festival` times FestivalGlow.darkness, a string lantern `line` times that. `color` is the light as it lands on the tinted picture: the light's own colour is divided by the tint (as NightView's shader does), at most `boost` times. A window's light hangs `out` cells in front of its pane, a stone lantern's `lamp_out` cells toward the camera from its fire box. range: cells; attenuation: the falloff's curve.
_background: The sky behind the land in the 3D view outdoors (Main3D's clear colour, Game.sky_color; rooms and mine floors keep their own background). keys: [minute of the day, colour], linear in between: dawn purple to peach at 6:30, a morning blue, the day blue 8fc6e8 (the colour the view had before) from 10:00 to 16:00, a golden 17:30, mauve at dusk 18:30, a deep blue night from 20:30 to 4:30. Under cloud the colour is greyed by cloud_grey (times 1 - the weather's sun value, weather_fx.json) and then times the weather tint, so rain and storms look greyer and darker.
_sprites: The world's light on the unshaded pixel sprites of the 3D view (SpriteLight). ref: the plain noon sun (sun.plain's colour, Main3D SUN_COLOR); a sprite is multiplied by the sun's colour over ref per channel (at most 1), `share` of the way from white, so noon, the night, rooms, mines and clouded days (the plain colour) leave the sprites as drawn and the golden morning and evening warm them by holding back green and blue, never brightening (nothing washes out). Why 0.45: the lit meshes take the whole sun colour; the sprites carry their own drawn light, so less than half keeps the faces and clothes reading in their own colours while the figure sits in the same golden hour as the houses behind it. lift: at night NightLights draws each figure near a lit window, shoji door, stone lantern or festival light back over the tint with `color` x the lift added in proportion to its own colour (its picture's pixel, so a pool already under it is not counted twice), so it reads warm by the light and stays night blue in the dark; the field's crops, cluster plants, items and objects take the same lift (measured at their picture's middle) in their own pass before the pools, only on the pixels where the tinted picture shows that picture's own pixel within `match` (the largest channel difference, 0..1: a little over the 8-bit steps and the faint bloom of the night picture, well under the gap between two different colours), so whatever stands in front keeps its own pixels. Each light within `range` cells of the figure's middle gives its energy (window / lamp times the windows' glow, festival times FestivalGlow.darkness, a string lantern `line` times that) times (1 - distance / range)^2; a window only to its lit side, its light `out` cells in front of the pane; a solid building between drops it; the sum is capped at `max`.
